files.lesson.md: --- order: 5 unit: volume node: AC9M7M02 n2 uses: [AC9M7M01 n1] # area of triangles title: Prisms and capacity summary: "Any right prism has the same shape all the way along: its cross-section. Volume = area of the cross-section × length, for triangles too (halve first). Capacity: 1 cm³ holds 1 mL, and 1000 cm³ is a litre." language: maths voice: { name: af_heart, speed: 1.1 } hook: "A tent, a chocolate bar in a triangular box, a drink carton: how much do they hold? If the shape is the same all the way through, one rule finds them all." connection: garden-bed-soil # data/connections/maths.yml app: command: node "$REPO_ROOT/tools/serve.mjs" "$REPO_ROOT/dist/_playground-board" 8277 url: http://127.0.0.1:8277/index.html readySelector: "#sl-h" layout: full explainPicture: { ref: prism.yml#explain-pic, caption: "The triangle is half of a 4 by 3 rectangle: 6 cm². 5 layers of it: $6 \\times 5 = 30$ cm³." } explainClip: query: { code: "@prism.yml#explain", fresh: 1, id: explain } caption: "The same all the way along" say: "A prism repeats its cross-section." clip: - caption: { text: "The triangle end: half of 4 × 3, so 6 cm².", say: "The triangle end is half of four by three: six square centimetres." } - wait: 1200 - caption: { text: "Each layer is another 6 cm³.", say: "Each layer adds another six." } - click: Make the height bigger - click: Make the height bigger - click: Make the height bigger - click: Make the height bigger - expect: { selector: "#gsum", contains: "= 30" } - wait: 600 - caption: { text: "V = 6 × 5 = 30 cm³.", say: "Six times five: thirty cubic centimetres." } - wait: 1200 --- A **right prism** has the same shape all the way through, like a loaf of bread: cut it anywhere, straight across, and you get the same slice. That slice is the **cross-section**. A box has a rectangle cross-section; a **triangular prism** (a tent, a triangular chocolate box) has a triangle. ## Predict: a triangular prism ```step stage: predict insight: "Committing to a volume for a triangular prism shows whether they halve for the triangle or multiply the three lengths as for a box." check: type: predict q: "A prism's triangle end is half of a 4 cm by 3 cm rectangle. The prism is 5 cm long. What is its volume?" options: ["30 cm³", "60 cm³", "12 cm³", "6 cm³"] actual: "30 cm³. The triangle is ½ × 4 × 3 = 6 cm², and 5 layers of 6 is 30. 60 is the whole box; 6 is one layer." ``` What is the area of the triangle end? ## Run: build the prism ```step stage: run insight: "Building the triangular prism up shows each layer is the triangle's area, half of the matching box's layer." try: { playground: board, starter: "prism.yml#run", height: 560 } check: { type: board, text: "Build the prism up to 5 cm. What is each layer, and the whole volume? Was your prediction right?", when: "h = 5", explain: "Each layer is the triangle, 6 cm². 5 layers: 30 cm³, half of the 4 by 3 by 5 box." } ``` The board stands the prism on its triangle end, so its length points up (h on the board). The orange triangle is the cross-section: half of a 4 by 3 rectangle, cut along its diagonal. Here's why the layers give the volume. The layer idea works for every prism. Each layer is the cross-section, and the layers go all the way along: $$V = \text{area of the cross-section} \times \text{length}$$ Volume and **capacity** (how much a container holds) are linked: 1 cm³ holds 1 millilitre, so 1000 cm³ holds 1 litre. ## Investigate: cross-section times length ```step stage: investigate insight: "V = cross-section area × length; Lena forgets the triangle's half. The cross-section is the face that repeats all the way along, not the biggest face." tasks: - check: type: answer q: "A prism's cross-section is a triangle with base 6 cm and height 4 cm. The prism is 10 cm long. What is its volume, in cm³?" answer: "120" feedback: - ["240", "Halve the triangle: ½ × 6 × 4 = 12."] - ["20", "That adds the lengths."] explain: "½ × 6 × 4 = 12 cm², × 10 = 120 cm³." - check: type: bug code: "working.txt#lena" text: "Lena finds how much air is inside a tent. Click the line where her working goes wrong." answer: 2 fault: logic misconception: triangle-no-half explain: "Line 2: the end is a triangle, so halve: ½ × 2 × 1.5 = 1.5 m². Volume = 1.5 × 3 = 4.5 m³." - check: type: question q: "How do you find a prism's cross-section?" options: ["It is the face that is the same shape all the way along, like a slice of bread", "It is always the face it stands on", "It is the biggest face"] answer: 0 feedback: [null, "A tent stands on a rectangle, but its cross-section is the triangle end.", "The biggest face of a tent is a sloping rectangle; the slices are triangles."] explain: "Cut straight across anywhere: the cross-section is what every slice looks like." ``` ### Any prism Here is the rule for any prism, and capacity. ```worked A = \tfrac{1}{2} \times 6 \times 4 = 12 \text{ cm}^2 :: Find the area of the cross-section (a triangle: halve). V = 12 \times 10 = 120 \text{ cm}^3 :: Times the length: one layer of 12 for each centimetre. 120 \text{ cm}^3 = 120 \text{ mL} :: Capacity: 1 cm³ holds 1 mL. 1000 \text{ cm}^3 = 1 \text{ L} :: 1000 mL is a litre: a 10 cm cube holds 1 L. ``` Now try one: a triangle end with base 6 cm and height 4 cm, 10 cm long. ### Find the mistake Read Lena's working. What shape is the tent's end? ### The cross-section ## Modify: one change at a time ```step stage: modify insight: "One change at a time: a 1 litre box on the board, cm³ to litres, a carton in mL, a parallelogram cross-section, then a prism standing differently." try: { playground: board, starter: "prism.yml#litre", height: 600 } tasks: - starter: "prism.yml#litre" hint: ["1 L = 1000 cm³.", "Try the same number for all three lengths."] check: { type: board, text: "Make a box that holds exactly 1 litre.", when: "v = 1000", explain: "10 × 10 × 10 = 1000 cm³ = 1000 mL = 1 L." } - check: type: answer q: "A container holds 2500 cm³. How many litres is that?" answer: "2.5" feedback: - ["2500", "That is millilitres. 1000 mL = 1 L."] - ["25", "Divide by 1000, not 100."] explain: "2500 ÷ 1000 = 2.5 L." - check: type: answer q: "A drink carton is 6 cm by 6 cm by 20 cm. How many millilitres does it hold?" answer: "720" feedback: - ["32", "That adds the lengths."] explain: "6 × 6 × 20 = 720 cm³ = 720 mL." - check: type: answer q: "A prism's cross-section is a parallelogram with base 5 cm and height 2 cm. The prism is 4 cm long. Volume, in cm³?" answer: "40" feedback: - ["20", "A parallelogram is not halved: 5 × 2 = 10 cm²."] explain: "5 × 2 = 10 cm², × 4 = 40 cm³." - check: type: question q: "Edge case: a triangular prism lies on its side, with its triangle end facing you. Does its volume change?" options: ["No: the cross-section and the length are the same", "Yes: it is now shorter", "Yes: the base is now a rectangle"] answer: 0 feedback: [null, "Turning it does not change the space inside.", "It stands on a rectangle, but the cross-section is still the triangle."] explain: "However it is turned, V = area of the triangle × length." ``` ### One litre Each task changes one thing. ### Litres ### Millilitres ### A parallelogram ### Turned over ## Practise: prisms ```step stage: practise insight: "A triangular prism, a capacity conversion and a box in mL, mixed; forgetting the half is the planted slip; the review keeps units fresh." tasks: - check: type: answer q: "A prism's cross-section has area 15 cm² and the prism is 8 cm long. Volume, in cm³?" answer: "120" feedback: - ["23", "That adds."] explain: "15 × 8 = 120 cm³." - check: type: answer q: "How many cm³ is 3 litres?" answer: "3000" feedback: - ["300", "1 L = 1000 cm³."] explain: "3 × 1000 = 3000 cm³." - check: type: answer q: "A tent's triangle end has base 3 m and height 2 m. It is 4 m long. Volume, in m³?" answer: "12" feedback: - ["24", "Halve the triangle: ½ × 3 × 2 = 3 m²."] explain: "3 m² × 4 = 12 m³." - check: type: answer q: "Review: write 250 cm in metres." answer: "2.5" feedback: - ["25", "100 cm = 1 m, so divide by 100."] explain: "250 ÷ 100 = 2.5 m." ``` ### Cross-section given ### Litres to cm³ ### A tent ### Review: units ## Make: a 24 cm³ wedge ```step stage: make insight: "Building a triangular prism with a set volume means the box it is half of must be 48: the halving works backwards." try: { playground: board, starter: "prism.yml#make", height: 580 } hint: ["The triangular prism is half a box. What volume must the box be?", "l × w × h = 48."] check: { type: board, text: "Build a triangular prism with volume 24 cm³.", when: "v = 24", explain: "l × w × h must be 48: for example 4, 3, 4 or 6, 2, 4 or 4, 4, 3." } ``` Then find one that is as long as possible. ## Make: soil for a corner bed, on paper ```step stage: make insight: "A triangular bed is a triangular prism lying flat: the floor is the cross-section and the soil depth is the length, so halve first." hint: ["Which shape stays the same all the way down through the soil?", "The two sides at the right angle are the triangle's base and height."] check: type: reasoning paper: true q: "A triangular garden bed fits into a corner. Its two straight sides at the right angle are 2 m and 1.5 m long, and it is filled with soil 0.4 m deep. How many cubic metres of soil fill it to the top?" steps: - ["The bed is a triangular prism: the floor is the triangle, and it is 0.4 m deep", "the same shape all the way down, so cross-section × depth"] - ["Triangle $= \\tfrac{1}{2} \\times 2 \\times 1.5 = 1.5$ m²", "the two sides at the right angle are the base and height"] - ["$V = 1.5 \\times 0.4 = 0.6$ m³", "cross-section area × depth"] picks: - step: 2 q: "Why is the floor 1.5 m² and not 3 m²?" options: - "A triangle is half of the 2 × 1.5 rectangle" - "Soil settles, so you take some off" - "The bed is only 1.5 m wide" answer: 0 feedback: [null, "Settling is a reason to order a little extra, not to change the floor's area.", "Both sides count: the triangle is cut from a 2 m by 1.5 m rectangle."] answer: "0.6" tolerance: 0 feedback: - ["1.2", "That treats the bed as a rectangle, 2 × 1.5 × 0.4. The floor is a triangle: halve."] - ["1.5", "That is the area of the floor. Multiply by the depth."] criteria: - "I found the shape that repeats all the way down, and halved for the triangle." - "My lengths are all in metres." - "My answer is in m³." explain: "The triangle floor is ½ × 2 × 1.5 = 1.5 m². With soil 0.4 m deep, V = 1.5 × 0.4 = 0.6 m³. Suppliers suggest ordering a little extra, because soil settles." ``` Do this one in your book, not on the screen. The bed is made up for the task. Sketch the triangle, work out the soil in cubic metres, and type it. **Also used in** - **Garden beds.** Soil is sold by the cubic metre, and suppliers suggest ordering a little extra because it settles. - **Concrete paths.** A path is a long, thin slab: its cross-section times its length, ordered in cubic metres. - **Tents.** The space inside a triangular tent is a triangular prism. ```teacher summary: Students build triangular prisms in layers, find volume as cross-section area × length for any right prism, and link volume to capacity (1 cm³ = 1 mL, 1000 cm³ = 1 L) (AC9M7M02, node 2). time: 40 timing: Predict and Run 8 min · Investigate 12 min · Modify 10 min · Practise and Make 10 min goals: - I can find the cross-section of a prism. - I can find the volume of a triangular prism. - I can change between cm³, mL and litres. struggle: Spotting the cross-section of a prism lying on its side. Ask students to imagine slicing it like bread and describe the slice, rather than pointing to the face for them. before: > Do the Run board yourself first. Students need V = A × h for boxes (previous lesson) and triangle area (Area unit). The one idea: every right prism is its cross-section repeated along its length, so V = cross-section area × length. The common mistake is forgetting the triangle's half (Lena's mistake, a spiral of the triangles lesson). Capacity conversions (mL, L) are new. running: - "Predict: students who chose 60 found the box, not the prism." - "Run: ask what the dashed rectangle on the floor shows." - "Investigate: hold up a triangular box or a tent picture and ask what a slice looks like." - "Modify: for the edge case, turn a real prism over." - "Make: ask why l × w × h must be 48." - "Paper: the corner bed is worked in books. Books out; look for the halving on the floor before the depth, and ask how much extra to order (soil settles)." stuck: - see: A student multiplies the three lengths of a triangular prism (Lena's mistake). ask: What shape is the slice? What is its area? fix: Halve for the triangle, then multiply by the length. - see: A student calls the face it stands on the cross-section. ask: If you slice it like bread, what shape is each slice? fix: The cross-section is the slice that repeats. - see: A student divides by 100 for litres. ask: How many mL in a litre? fix: 1000 mL = 1 L, and 1 cm³ = 1 mL. stretch: A swimming pool is a prism whose cross-section is a trapezium (shallow to deep end). Estimate how many litres it holds. support: Use real prisms and slices of play dough; write the cross-section area first, every time. leads: > Next: Circles (AC9M7M03). Where it leads: volume of cylinders (Year 9), where the cross-section is a circle, and surface area of prisms. exit: q: A prism's triangle end has base 5 cm and height 4 cm; it is 6 cm long. Find its volume and its capacity in mL. a: ½ × 5 × 4 = 10 cm², × 6 = 60 cm³ = 60 mL. explain: > A **right prism** has the same cross-section all the way along. Its volume is that slice's area times the length: $$V = A \times h$$ For a triangular prism, the cross-section is a triangle: halve first ($\tfrac{1}{2} \times 6 \times 4 = 12$ cm², then $\times 10 = 120$ cm³). **Capacity:** 1 cm³ holds 1 mL, and 1000 cm³ = 1 L. ```
